# What a class factory does

robjc declares classes through four factories instead of calling `R6::R6Class()` directly.
Each factory obtains an R6 generator and configures its `isa` identity, protocol contracts, and instance creation path.
This note (04) follows that implementation sequence.
For the public arguments and examples, see the [class factory guide](guide_05_ClassFactory.Rmd).

| Factory | Creates | Additional setup |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `RSObjectClass()` | Ordinary object class | Parent class, adopted protocols, `$new()` |
| `RSSingletonClass()` | Class with a shared instance | One `$instance` |
| `RSScalarClass()` | Scalar and its NA subclass | Shared NA instance, class cluster |
| `RSProtocolClass()` | Protocol generator | Parent protocols, required methods, no instances |

## Resolve the superclass generator

R evaluates function arguments lazily.
An R6 generator's `inherit` may therefore retain an expression for its parent.
The ordinary, Singleton, and Scalar factories first evaluate `super_generator <- force(super_class)` to obtain the actual parent generator.
They pass this reference to `R6Class()` as `inherit` and store it in `isa$super`, allowing the robjc runtime to traverse parent generators directly.

```{r eval=FALSE}
super_generator <- force(super_class)
klass <- do.call(R6::R6Class, list(
  classname = class_name,
  inherit = super_generator,
  class = FALSE,
  cloneable = FALSE,
  public = public,
  private = private,
  parent_env = parent_env
))
```

This excerpt presents the central part of ordinary class creation.
The actual code also validates arguments, and `RSObjectClass()` passes the class name as a positional argument.
At the R6 level, a protocol inherits from `RSProtocol`; its potentially multiple parent protocols are recorded in `isa` as `super_protocols`.
R6's single inheritance and declared protocol inheritance use separate paths.

## The result of `do.call(R6::R6Class, ...)`

`do.call()` returns the R6 class generator as `klass`.
The factory retains it before calling `robjc_make_isa()`, so it can store the generator itself in `isa$class`.
It also stores the previously resolved parent generator in `isa$super`.
Instances refer to this same `isa` environment through their private `.__isa` field.
See [note 01](tech_01_isa.Rmd) for the reference structure and inheritance chain.

```{r}
library(robjc)

Parent <- RSObjectClass("Tech04Parent")
Child <- RSObjectClass("Tech04Child", super_class = Parent)
child <- Child$new()

stopifnot(identical(Child$robjc_isa$class, Child))
stopifnot(identical(Child$robjc_isa$super, Parent))
stopifnot(identical(child$class(), Child))
stopifnot(child$isKindOf(Parent))
```

## Options passed to R6

`RSObjectClass()` passes `class = FALSE` and `cloneable = FALSE`.
With `class = FALSE`, R6 does not add its own `R6` marker to instances; robjc sets S3 classes along the inheritance chain.
With `cloneable = FALSE`, copying follows robjc's `copy()` and `mutableCopy()` contracts instead of R6's standard `clone()`.
The factory has no public `active` argument, so its standard declaration path cannot specify R6 active bindings.
It does not set `portable` explicitly and uses R6's default of `TRUE`.
Consequently, methods resolve `self`, `private`, and `super` through environments, and `robjc_allocate()` reconstructs the same references.

The Singleton and Scalar factories also pass `class = FALSE` and `cloneable = FALSE` when creating R6 generators.
The protocol factory passes both options and additionally sets `lock_class = TRUE`.

## `isa`, S3 markers, and protocol contracts

`robjc_make_isa()` creates an environment containing `class`, `super`, `protocols`, `slot`, and `version`.
It places this environment in the generator's `robjc_isa` binding and in the private `.__isa` field definition.
It also adds the `RSObjectIsA` or `RSProtocolIsA` S3 marker to `isa`, and the `RobjcClass` marker to the generator.
See [note 03](tech_03_ObjectType.Rmd) for the type predicates that use these markers.

An ordinary class records adopted protocols, including inherited declarations, in `isa$protocols`.
When `validate_protocols = TRUE`, `protocol_getMissingContracts(klass)` finds missing public method names and stops class declaration if any are absent.
This check does not verify method signatures or behavior.

```{r}
Runnable <- RSProtocolClass("Tech04Runnable", contract_methods = "run")
Runner <- RSObjectClass("Tech04Runner",
  protocols = list(Runnable),
  public = list(run = function() "done")
)
stopifnot(identical(protocol_getMissingContracts(Runner), character(0)))
stopifnot(Runner$new()$conformsTo(Runnable))
```

For `RSScalarClass()`, both the ordinary class and its NA subclass are subject to contract validation.
`RSProtocolClass()` stores required method names in `isa$slot`, but the protocol itself need not implement them.

## Singleton, Protocol, and Scalar `isa` slots

A Singleton passes through `robjc_make_singleton_isa()`, which first attaches an ordinary `isa` and then creates the shared instance.
It stores that instance in `Class$instance` and `Class$robjc_isa$slot`, and adds the `RobjcSingleton` marker to the generator.

A Protocol passes through `protocol_make_isa()`, which stores parent protocols in `isa$protocols` and directly required method names in `isa$slot`.
The factory removes method names already required by parent protocols from the direct requirements.
Its generator has an `RSProtocolIsA` `isa`, distinguishing it from an ordinary object class.

A Scalar factory creates an ordinary class and then its NA subclass.
It stores the shared NA instance in the ordinary class's `isa$slot` and `$na`.
See [note 06](tech_06_Scalars.Rmd) for NA class generation and the class cluster.

```{r}
Shared <- RSSingletonClass("Tech04Shared")
stopifnot(identical(Shared$robjc_isa$slot, Shared$instance))
stopifnot(identical(Runnable$robjc_isa$slot, "run"))
stopifnot(identical(RSNumber$robjc_isa$slot, RSNumber$na))
```

## Adjusting `$new()` and locking

The ordinary class factory calls `robjc_install_new(klass)` to replace R6's `$new()`.
The replacement allocates an instance with `robjc_allocate(klass)`, calls its `initialize(...)`, and returns that result.
The reason for separating allocation and initialization is explained in [note 02](tech_02_new_initialize.Rmd).

A Singleton is created once during class declaration; later `$new()` calls return that shared instance.
A Protocol cannot be instantiated, so its R6 `$new` binding is set to `NULL` and locked.
After creating a shared instance, an NA Singleton class replaces direct `$new()` calls with an error.

Finally, `robjc_freeze_isa()` locks the `isa` environment and the generator's `robjc_isa` binding to protect the established class identity.
For classes shipped with the package, `.onLoad()` reapplies the necessary locks after lazy loading.

```{r}
stopifnot(environmentIsLocked(Child$robjc_isa))
stopifnot(bindingIsLocked("robjc_isa", Child))
stopifnot(is.null(Runnable$new))
stopifnot(bindingIsLocked("new", Runnable))
```
